issue_context.title: Modbus frozen if one or more devices are unavailable
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Might be a dup of #51027, but unfortunately nothing is really known about the setup mentioned here, so I am opening up a new issue.

I am running the latest beta `2021.6.0b2` and now lovelace will load and is quite responsive, but unfortunately the modbus bus is still dead if one or more devices are missing/unresponsive. This might be due to the constant retrying, introduced by the *unconfigurable* option in 1b3f9254bc5b392c29a3219bb1b82d127036d18c.

At least now lovelace shows the status of the device and shows that it is `not available`, so that is already a good way to find out which devices to get to and either uncomment from the configuration so that hass does not try to connect to them or otherwise make them them available on the bus, eg fixing the actual modbus device:
![Bildschirmfoto von 2021-06-01 10-42-59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1778889/120294560-9ab81300-c2c6-11eb-92e2-63a6d00356b6.png)

I then tried setting a timeout, because my expectation was that it would then give up on a device after 0.5s and not retry the same transaction some more times, but unfortunately it is ignored and still retried several times, as you can see in the log.

The loop of refreshing dead devices goes on forever and unfortunately writing to devices (coils or registers) eg setting a fan, light or switch will not take priority and in my case not be executed/sent for some hours, maybe even never.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.6.0b2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2021.1.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/

At first it will go through all of the devices, get their status and mark them unavailable if they are, but unfortunately this will not take 0.5s per device which would be acceptable, but almost two minutes per device. This can get out of hand quickly and render the bus unusable.
comments:
Hey there @adamchengtkc, @janiversen, @vzahradnik, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`modbus`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L302) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Setting timeout to 0.3 is way below the recommended limit for modbus serial, especially with 9.600bps, alone the traffic delay is about 1 second. Modbus recommends a timeout of 10 seconds. I see however that you found a bug in the validator, who should have catched this.

Looking at your log the timeout is 14 seconds (look at line 5-6 in the log).

You are wrong about the commit, timeout for serial is configurable see https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/modbus/modbus.py line 217.

Your problem is real, but so far I have not been able to find a suitable algorithm to solve it:
- if a device do not respond, we stop polling all platforms of the device, easy to do and you have no delay, but it would mean you need to restart ha to get them back online.
- special case a single platform in a device do not respond, most likely due to a misconfiguration, same procedure as above.
- once a device if unavailable try it inly sometimes. The problem here is to define sometimes. Scan_interval would be natural but we have configurations that uses 9999 (or the new 0).

So while I see and know your problem I still fail to see an elegant solution.

> Setting timeout to 0.3 is way below the recommended limit for modbus serial, especially with 9.600bps, alone the traffic delay is about 1 second. Modbus recommends a timeout of 10 seconds.

Good to know! Usually my modbus devices respond much faster and in general the system works when I set the timeout to 0.5s.

> You are wrong about the commit, timeout for serial is configurable see https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/modbus/modbus.py line 217.

I never said anything about that. What I mentioned is the retry option for modbus serial. Is that configurable but undocumented?

> Your problem is real, but so far I have not been able to find a suitable algorithm to solve it:
> 
>     * if a device do not respond, we stop polling all platforms of the device, easy to do and you have no delay, but it would mean you need to restart ha to get them back online.

Not a good option, correct.

>     * special case a single platform in a device do not respond, most likely due to a misconfiguration, same procedure as above.

If a misconfiguration results in a syntactically correct config object, then it's all good. If devices get added that are unavailable, hass should not be able to distinguish between a misconfiguration and unavailable devices, so yes, same procedure as for unavailable devices. Still not recommended to require an entire restart of hass though, so same as above.

>     * once a device if unavailable try it inly sometimes. The problem here is to define sometimes. Scan_interval would be natural but we have configurations that uses 9999 (or the new 0).

Well, in that case the scan_interval is misused, no? Since modbus depends on polling, technically a modbus master can not be informed "via some sort of push" method. So scan_interval needs to be set to some sane value.

> So while I see and know your problem I still fail to see an elegant solution.

I do not think it is a problem to include unavailable devices in the loop. But spending almost two minutes trying to retry is just insane.

I am quite certain, that once we stop polling the device three or four times, and block the bus for that time, it will be good. I do not really know what you were trying to solve with #34678 / the commit I actually mentioned above, but IMO if you introduce this option, it needs to be configurable, because in a case like this with offline devices, I really really do not want to poll them in this loop.
I want to give each modbus device a chance to respond until `timeout` expires and if no response has been received, that's it in that loop. Next loop next chance. I really want to prevent any kind of blocking in my polling loop.

I had a quick look at the issues you mentioned in your PR, that you were trying to fix with your PR. It might have fixed them, but there might have been another way to fix them and this at the same time.

What do you think?

In the meantime, maybe we could just have an config entry to disable the retires?

```
I never said anything about that. What I mentioned is the retry option for modbus serial. Is that configurable but undocumented?
```
In the PR you wrote “ introduced by the unconfigurable option in 1b3f925.”, and I simply responded it it configurable (and also documented) as the timeout: parameter.

```
Well, in that case the scan_interval is misused, no? Since modbus depends on polling, technically a modbus master can not be informed "via some sort of push" method. So scan_interval needs to be set to some sane value.
```
No it is not a misuse, scan_interval: 0 have some good usage, the simplest example is a switch, where you can avoid polling, unless you turn it on/off in that case we do a poll to verify the new state.
We had another request, where a user wanted only to poll based on a script, scan_interval: 0 together with a service call did that. 
```
I do not really know what you were trying to solve with #34678 / the commit 
```
As the title says allow retries. Sometimes 0 bytes is received, “retry_on_empty” tells the library to retry within the timeout.

Disabling the retries is a very bad idea, because RS485, have frequent retries. On my test system I see 2-3 pr hour, but the sensor keeps a correct value. Disable the retries would mean a lot more unavailable.

review_comments: Are these options only applicable to the serial client or to all client types?

Right now I have only activated it for serial, because I had a user that was lost without this change. Next week I will test it on the other communications as well.

I could have added it in the serial schema, but then I would have to change the schema next week, I preferred to have this general….test the other communications and add it to them. Anyhow this PR will not be released before 2021.7 so there are plenty of time.

If you insist I can add parameters to other communications in this PR, the parameters are allowed but I have not tested the implementation.
The config validation should be as precise as possible. Please adjust it.
